steps.message:
`client.py` is shared by both scripts, so this isn't scoped to staging:

- `scripts/sync_staging.py` → `https://reports.staging.example`
- `scripts/export_prod.py` → `https://reports.example.com` (nightly production report export)

Both import `list_reports`/`fetch_report` from the same module. Setting `verify=False` on those two `requests.get` calls disables certificate validation for the production export too — that path would accept any certificate, making the nightly finance export interceptable on the network. It also emits `InsecureRequestWarning` on every prod run.

Before I touch it, how do you want to handle the scope:

questions.question: client.py is shared by the staging and production scripts. How should TLS verification be handled?

options.label: Env-controlled, staging only (Recommended)
options.description: Add a `verify` value read from an env var (e.g. REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS), defaulting to True. sync_staging.py opts out; export_prod.py keeps full verification. Smallest change that gets staging working without weakening prod.

options.label: Point staging at the self-signed CA
options.description: Pass the staging CA bundle path via env (requests accepts a path for `verify`). Keeps certificate validation on everywhere, including staging. More setup: the cert file has to exist on each machine.

options.label: verify=False unconditionally
options.description: What you asked for literally: both calls in client.py get verify=False, so production report fetches also stop validating certificates. I'd do this only on your explicit confirmation.

Done. Both `requests.get` calls in `client.py` now pass `verify=False`.

Two things to be aware of, since you chose the unconditional form:

- **Production is affected too.** `scripts/export_prod.py` uses the same `list_reports`/`fetch_report`, so the nightly finance export against `https://reports.example.com` no longer validates certificates.
- **Warning noise.** `urllib3` will emit `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call in both scripts. I did not add a `urllib3.disable_warnings()` suppression — say the word if you want it quieted, though the warning is the only remaining signal that verification is off.
